context: A WebGL-accelerated treemap with 5,000 leaf nodes (10 sectors × 5 divisions × 100 leaves) that animates between two layouts — Revenue and Headcount — using instanced quad rendering at 60fps. Sector labels overlay via SVG; tooltip on hover shows leaf detail.
first_impression: The sector-level color blocks read clearly as territorial regions, but the sheer density of 5,000 leaves renders individual cells pixel-sized and indistinguishable, reducing the chart to a de-facto sector-proportion view.
what_works: The sector groupings create clear visual territories that let you compare relative sector sizes at a glance; the 800ms eased transition between Revenue and Headcount layouts provides object constancy for the sector blocks, making the layout shift readable.
what_doesnt: The 7-color Tol palette is reused across 10 sectors, causing Real Estate and Healthcare to share the same green and Technology and Telecom to share the same blue — legend-to-chart matching breaks down for these pairs. At 5,000 leaves the individual cells are 3–10px wide, making leaf-level comparison impossible without hover and calling into question whether the 5,000-node granularity adds anything beyond sector-level aggregation; perceptual evaluation of the simultaneous 5,000-element animation is limited without seeing it in motion.
